profile.reading:
This facility, "Miejska Sieć Komputerowa CzestMAN" (City Computer Network CzestMAN), is a real academic and research computing network operated by Częstochowa University of Technology (Politechnika Częstochowska) at ul. Dąbrowskiego 71 in Częstochowa, Poland. The prior record for this facility carried no operator name; this registry corrects that gap directly. Despite the "municipal network" implication in its historic name, this is an academic institutional facility rather than a city-government-operated one, per the operator's own site.

CzestMAN provides cloud computing services for Polish science and education, along with eduroam wireless authentication, EduVPN, e-learning platform hosting, and data storage services, and participates in national Polish research computing initiatives including PIONIER, PRACE-LAB, and KMD4EOSC, per its own site. This positions it within Poland's broader academic and research computing network (MAN, or Metropolitan Area Network) infrastructure, a category distinct from commercial colocation or hyperscale cloud operators.

As an academic institutional facility, CzestMAN does not publish commercial-style IT capacity, technical square footage, or year-opened figures for public marketing purposes in the way commercial colocation providers do; no such figures were found in sourcing available this session. Poland's national research and education network infrastructure, of which CzestMAN is a regional node, has grown substantially over the past two decades to support the country's universities and research institutes, a distinct category worth noting alongside the commercial operators (Data4, T-Mobile Poland, and others) tracked elsewhere in this registry's Polish facility rows. Per its own operator page, CzestMAN runs about 31 kilometers of fiber optic lines, split between roughly 7.5 kilometers and 21 kilometers of leased and owned telecom ducting, across 6 primary nodes, including the main CzestMAN hub and a PIONIER national research network node, plus 13 secondary nodes, and it integrates the computer networks of four higher education institutions in Czestochowa. Czestochowa University of Technology itself was founded in 1949 as a School of Engineering and renamed Politechnika Czestochowska in 1955, marking its 75th anniversary in 2024, though this founding date describes the parent university rather than the CzestMAN network specifically.
